content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (especially near -0.21 or below) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Model consistently overpredicts the first 5–7 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when sentiment is rising or neutral.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-period, model fails to adjust downward — true prices often dip sharply after a peak.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts too long after a spike, ignoring recent price pullback.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses the true price’s peak or trough by 2–5 days, especially when sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment is rising but price is flat or falling, model tends to ignore the trend and overreacts later — forecast becomes too bullish.
- Model underreacts to sentiment shifts in the last 3–5 days of the 18-day history — true price often reacts more sharply than forecasted.
